textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 10 social-science · Economics 1: Development · Textbook Concepts
textbookBox.concept: Different people have different developmental goals. What is development for one may be unfair for another, and people often seek income, security, respect and freedom together.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: A common measure is average income, also called per capita income, which is the total income of a country divided by its total population.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 10 social-science · Economics 1: Development · Deeper Textbook Ideas
textbookBox.concept: Income alone is not enough. Public facilities like health, education and a public distribution system also matter, and the Human Development Report of UNDP compares countries using health, education

beats.en: Income alone is not enough. Public facilities like health, education and a public distribution system also matter, and the Human Development Report of UNDP compares countries using health, education and income.
beats.speakEn: Income alone is not enough. Public facilities like health, education and a public distribution system also matter, and the Human Development Report of UNDP compares countries using health, education and income.

beats.en: Kerala has a low infant mortality rate and high literacy, though its per capita income is lower than that of states such as Haryana. So higher income does not always mean better human development.
beats.speakEn: Kerala has a low infant mortality rate and high literacy, though its per capita income is lower than that of states such as Haryana. So higher income does not always mean better human development.
